issues.legal_issue: The statutory power to lease public property on imposed terms is not invalidated by the failure to make rules governing those terms.
material_facts: The governing statute authorized the government to sell, lease, or otherwise transfer public property on terms and conditions it considered fit to impose.
Rules contemplated by the statute had not been framed when the leases and rent increases at issue were made.
The tenants ultimately conceded that the government had power to lease the property and impose conditions without first framing rules.
issues.conclusion: The absence of rules did not make the leases or their terms, including the rent enhancement at issue, illegal, void, or inoperative.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3 and 22 of the Capital of Punjab (Development & Regulation) Act, 1952, read together, authorize the government to transfer property on terms it considers fit and contemplate rules regulating those terms. Failure to make rules does not itself invalidate a transfer or its terms.

predicates.public_property_lease_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a government lease of public property.
predicates.statutory_transfer_power_exists: The governing law authorizes the government to transfer the property on terms and conditions it imposes.
predicates.rules_not_framed: The government had not made the contemplated rules when it leased the property or imposed the challenged terms.

issues.definition: When a public-property lease is authorized by law, the absence of contemplated rules does not by itself invalidate its terms.

issues.legal_issue: A government rent enhancement supported by a reasoned, consistently applied assessment is not arbitrary merely because it substantially increases the rent.
material_facts: The administration based its revised rent assessment on construction and land values, depreciation, a rental-value calculation, and a multiplier for commercial premises.
An official affidavit gave a detailed calculation supporting the revised rent.
The High Court found that the assessment procedure was not arbitrary, discriminatory, or unreasonable, and the Supreme Court agreed.
The administration said the revised approach was applied uniformly to similarly situated shopkeepers.
issues.conclusion: The rent enhancement was upheld because the assessment had a reasoned basis and was not shown to be arbitrary, discriminatory, or unreasonable.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 requires government action to be guided by rational, relevant, and non-discriminatory standards. Under Ramana Dayaram Shetty v. International Airport Authority of India and Kumari Shrilekha Vidyarthi v. State of U.P., public action, including contractual action, must not be arbitrary; judicial review examines the reasons and decision-making process and does not substitute the court’s own reasons for the government’s.

predicates.government_lease_rent_review: The proceeding reviews a government decision to increase rent under a lease.
predicates.reasoned_rent_assessment: The government supported its rent assessment with an explained method and relevant valuation factors.
predicates.assessment_applied_to_similar_lessees: The government applied the assessment approach to other lessees in comparable circumstances.

issues.definition: A rent increase is upheld when a government lease-rent review concerns an increase supported by an explained assessment applied to comparable lessees.

issues.legal_issue: Unequal treatment resulting from another person’s unchallenged rent is not a basis for relief unless that treatment was lawful and the cases are materially similar.
material_facts: The tenants argued that rent had not been enhanced for certain other occupants.
The other premises referred to were privately owned, and the tenants did not allege or establish that the failure to enhance rent for other government lessees was lawful or justified.
The tenants did not show that their circumstances were materially similar to those of persons who had received a lawful and justified treatment.
issues.conclusion: The tenants established no basis for an Article 14 discrimination claim based on the failure to enhance rent for others.
issues.legal_principle: Article 14 does not require an authority to repeat an unlawful or unwarranted action. Chandigarh Administration v. Jagjit Singh holds that an order benefiting another person supports a claim to similar relief only if that order was lawful and justified and the claimant’s case is similar in material respects.

rule.if: government_action_discrimination_claim and different_treatment_for_another_person and (other_treatment_not_shown_lawful or material_similarity_not_shown)

predicates.government_action_discrimination_claim: The proceeding challenges government action on the ground that another person received different treatment.
predicates.different_treatment_for_another_person: The claimant identifies another person who received more favorable treatment from the authority.
predicates.other_treatment_not_shown_lawful: The claimant does not establish that the other person’s favorable treatment was lawful and justified.
predicates.material_similarity_not_shown: The claimant does not establish that the relevant circumstances of the two cases are materially similar.

issues.definition: A claim based on another person’s more favorable treatment fails when its lawfulness or the material similarity of the cases is not established.

issues.legal_issue: A further enhancement of rent under the leases must not be made until the contemplated rules governing property transfers have been framed.
material_facts: The contemplated rules governing transfers of property and their terms had not been framed.
The Supreme Court directed that the rent of the tenants and similarly situated lessees not be further enhanced without those rules.
issues.conclusion: The rent must not be further enhanced until the contemplated rules are framed.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3 and 22 of the Capital of Punjab (Development & Regulation) Act, 1952, contemplate rules regulating property transfers. Although the absence of rules did not invalidate the existing leases or the enhancement considered in the appeals, the Court directed that further rent enhancement await the framing of rules.

predicates.government_lease_rent_proceeding: The proceeding concerns rent charged under a government lease.
predicates.further_rent_increase_proposed: The government proposes to increase the rent again for the leased property.
predicates.rules_not_framed: The government has not framed the contemplated rules governing property transfers and their terms.

issues.definition: A proposed further rent increase is deferred when it concerns a government lease and the contemplated rules have not been framed.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant who obtains an interim stay and ultimately loses the substantive proceeding remains liable for appropriate interest on rent withheld during the stay.
material_facts: The tenants obtained court orders staying payment of the enhanced rent.
The tenants’ substantive challenges were dismissed.
The High Court imposed interest at 18% per annum for the period during which payment was stayed.
The Supreme Court held that interest was payable for that period but reduced the rate to 15% per annum, considering the higher rate excessive.
issues.conclusion: The tenants were liable to pay appropriate interest on the rent withheld during the stay, at 15% per annum rather than 18%.
issues.legal_principle: A stay order does not confer an additional substantive right, and when the proceeding ends, the court should restore the parties, so far as possible, to the position they would have occupied without the interim order. Shree Chamundi Mopeds Ltd. v. Church of South India Trust Association and Kanoria Chemicals and Industries Ltd. v. U.P. State Electricity Board support liability for payment and interest on amounts withheld under a stay that is followed by dismissal; Kashyap Zip Industries v. Union of India likewise supports interest during the stay period. The rate must be just and not punitive.

predicates.court_stay_obtained: The tenant obtained an interim court order staying payment of rent.
predicates.rent_withheld_during_stay: The tenant withheld rent while the interim stay was in force.
predicates.substantive_challenge_dismissed: The court ultimately dismissed the tenant’s substantive challenge.

issues.definition: A tenant who withholds rent under an interim stay and loses the substantive challenge must pay appropriate interest on the withheld rent.

issues.legal_issue: An authority may charge appropriate interest on rent arrears that accrued before an interim stay, subject to acting fairly and justly in setting the rate.
material_facts: The High Court allowed appropriate interest on rent arrears from the date the enhanced rent became payable until the date the stay orders were made.
The Supreme Court agreed that the authority could charge appropriate interest for that pre-stay period and directed it to act fairly and justly in determining the rate.
issues.conclusion: The authority could charge appropriate interest on arrears accrued before the stay, with the rate to be determined fairly and justly.
issues.legal_principle: The Court distinguished arrears accrued before an interim stay from rent withheld because of the stay, and agreed that the authority could charge appropriate interest on the former, subject to fair and just determination.

predicates.government_lease_rent_proceeding: The proceeding concerns rent charged under a government lease.
predicates.rent_arrears_accrued_before_stay: The tenant owed rent before obtaining an interim order staying payment.

issues.definition: An authority may charge interest on pre-stay rent arrears if it determines the interest fairly and justly.

issues.legal_issue: Rent cannot be enhanced during a fixed contractual lease term when the lease does not authorize an increase during that term.
material_facts: A lessee’s lease ran for a fixed three-year term at a stated rent.
The lease provided for renewal for a further term at rent determined by the government, but did not authorize an increase during the initial three-year term.
The authority sought to apply the enhanced rent before that initial term expired.
issues.conclusion: The enhanced rent was not valid during the initial three-year term but was valid from the start of the renewal term; the lessee was entitled to pay the contractual rent during the initial term.
issues.legal_principle: The terms of the lease controlled during its fixed initial term. The provision allowing renewal at rent determined by the government applied to the renewal term, not to an increase during the initial term.

predicates.government_lease_rent_proceeding: The proceeding concerns rent charged under a government lease.
predicates.fixed_term_lease: The lease sets a fixed period during which the tenancy continues on stated terms.
predicates.rent_increase_not_authorized_during_fixe: The lease does not authorize the lessor to increase rent during the fixed term.

issues.definition: A rent increase is invalid during a fixed lease term when the lease does not authorize an increase during that term.
